part.text:
I read the model and cross-checked it against the parsed/validated structure (the Structurizr tools operate on an in-memory copy — the file on disk was only read, never written). It parses and validates cleanly, so there are no syntax errors; the findings below are about C4 modeling quality.

## Findings

- **`payments` (Payment Gateway) and `loyaltyFeed` (Loyalty Points Feed) — wrong element type.** Both are declared as generic `element`, not `softwareSystem`. In C4, external systems you integrate with are software systems. As generic elements they become "custom elements": they carry no system semantics, can't have their own context view, and C4 tooling won't treat them as systems. They should be `softwareSystem`.

- **`legacy` (Legacy Booking System) — disconnected and unviewed.** It has no relationships to/from it and appears on no view (the inspector flags both: "disconnected" and "not included on any views"). If it's truly retired it shouldn't be in the model; if it's being phased out (still active) the model should show the migration path. Its description ("The retired booking system being phased out") is also self-contradictory. As-is it's dead weight that misrepresents the architecture.

- **`rate` → `tariff` — impossible technology.** Rate Service is **Go**, Tariff Rules Library is **Python**, and the relationship is labeled "library call." A Go process cannot make a direct in-process call into a Python library. They must share a language, or the relationship must be a remote call (HTTP/gRPC).

- **`stays` → `staydb` — missing core persistence.** Stay Service "Registers and tracks stays" and Stay Database "Stores stay and room records," yet there is no relationship between them. The service that owns stay records never writes to the database that stores them — the central data path is absent.

- **`scheduler` (Batch Scheduler) — inconsistent with its purpose.** It "Runs the nightly rate and housekeeping batch" but has no relationships to `rate` or `housekeeping`. Its only link is `stays → scheduler` ("Registers nightly tasks in"), which doesn't show how the nightly batch actually reaches the Rate and Housekeeping services.

- **`notifications` (Notification Hub) — dead end.** It "Sends booking and stay messages" and receives events from the queue, but has no outbound relationship — the messages go to no one, not even the Guest.

- **`rooms` (Room Assignment) — dead end.** It "Assigns rooms to confirmed stays" but has no outbound relationship; the assignment is never persisted (e.g., to `staydb`, which "Stores stay and room records").

- **`reporting` (Reporting Service) — no consumer.** It reads from `staydb` and "Produces occupancy and revenue reports," but nothing in the model consumes those reports, and there is no person (e.g., a manager/operations role) to receive them.

- **`availability`, `deposits`, `feedback`, `concierge` — nothing triggers them.** Each has only outbound relationships and no inbound ones, so no part of the modeled flow invokes them: no one searches room availability, no booking step takes a deposit, no one submits feedback, and no guest request is routed to the concierge. Their described purposes aren't reflected in any relationship.

- **`guest` → `mobile` — broken description.** "Books through the app via" ends on a dangling "via" and isn't a complete phrase. It should read e.g. "Books stays through the mobile app."

- **`portal` → `rate` — vague description.** "uses" doesn't say what the portal uses the Rate Service for. It should read e.g. "Calculates stay rates via."

- **`documentstore` (Document Store) — name/technology mismatch.** It's named "Document Store" and described as holding "contracts, invoices, and media," but its technology is PostgreSQL (a relational DB).
